name: Comment-based Workflow

on:
  issue_comment:
    types:
      - created

jobs:
  process_comment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Parse Comment and Extract Branch
        id: extract
        run: |
          # Extract source branch info from comment
          comment_body=$(jq -r .comment.body $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH)
          source_branch=$(echo "$comment_body" | grep -o -P '(?<=source: ).*' | head -n 1)
          
          # Get list of open pull requests
          pull_requests=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            "https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls")

          # Extract pull request info and match source branch
          source_branch_found=false
          for pr in $(echo "$pull_requests" | jq -r '.[].head.ref'); do
            if [ "$pr" == "$source_branch" ]; then
              source_branch_found=true
              break
            fi
          done

          if [ "$source_branch_found" == "true" ]; then
            echo "::set-output name=source_branch::$source_branch"
          else
            echo "Source branch not found in open pull requests."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Display Extracted Branch
        run: |
          echo "Extracted Source Branch: ${{ steps.extract.outputs.source_branch }}"

Here are some steps you can take to address this situation:Understand Why Files in node_modules Are Marked as Changed:node_modules contains all the dependencies for your project, and these dependencies can frequently receive updates.The changes you see in node_modules are often related to updates in packages or their dependencies.Review Changes:Use the GitHub Desktop interface to review the specific changes made to the files in the node_modules directory. Look for changes in package versions, configuration files, or other relevant updates.Determine if Changes are Necessary:Not all changes in node_modules need to be committed. Generally, you don't commit changes in the node_modules directory because these dependencies can be easily reinstalled using package management tools like npm or yarn.Changes that should be committed typically include modifications to your project's configuration files (e.g., package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock) that specify the dependencies and their versions.Gitignore node_modules:To avoid accidentally committing changes in the node_modules directory, make sure you have a .gitignore file that excludes this directory from version control.If you haven't already done so, create or update your .gitignore file to include an entry for node_modules/. This will prevent Git from tracking changes in this directory.Example .gitignore entry:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Commit Only Necessary Changes:Commit the changes that are essential for your project, such as modifications to your source code, configuration files, or documentation.Avoid committing changes in the node_modules directory unless you have a specific reason to do so (e.g., you've made custom modifications to a library).Dependency Management:Instead of committing the entire node_modules directory, manage your project's dependencies using a package manager like npm or yarn.Use a package manager's lock file (e.g., package-lock.json or yarn.lock) to ensure consistent dependency versions across different development environments.When you clone your project on a new machine or share it with others, they can use the package manager to install the correct dependencies.Regularly Update Dependencies:Periodically update your project's dependencies to benefit from bug fixes, security updates, and new features. Conversations.Prompt: why there's another file called: package-lock.json, i already have a file named package.json
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTThe presence of both package.json and package-lock.json files in a Node.js project is standard and serves different purposes:package.json:package.json is a metadata file for your Node.js project. It contains information about your project, its dependencies, scripts for running various tasks, and other project-specific configurations.You manually manage the content of this file, specifying the dependencies your project requires, as well as their versions and other configuration details.package-lock.json:package-lock.json is an automatically generated file created by npm (Node Package Manager) when you run npm install or npm update. This file is used to lock down the specific versions of dependencies that your project is currently using.It ensures that everyone working on the project uses the exact same versions of dependencies to maintain consistency across development environments.It includes the specific versions of all direct and transitive dependencies (dependencies of dependencies) that your project relies on.It also contains information about the integrity of the installed packages to verify that they haven't been tampered with.The reason for having both files is to maintain version consistency across different development environments. Here's how they work together:When you add a dependency or run npm install, npm will update both package.json (to reflect the dependency) and package-lock.json (to specify the exact version and resolve dependencies).When someone else clones your project or when you deploy it to a different environment, they can run npm install, and npm will use the information in package-lock.json to install the exact same versions of dependencies that you were using when you initially created or updated the package-lock.json file.This ensures that even if new versions of packages are released, your project will use the versions that were known to work together when you initially set up the project. It helps prevent "dependency hell" and ensures consistent behavior across different environments.In summary, package.json is for you to specify your project's dependencies and other metadata, while package-lock.json is an automatically generated file that locks down the specific versions of those dependencies for consistent installations across different environments. Both files are essential for managing Node.js projects effectively.

Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTURLSearchParams는 웹 브라우저에서 URL의 쿼리 문자열을 다루기 위한 JavaScript의 내장 객체입니다. URL의 쿼리 문자열은 물음표(?) 다음에 키-값 쌍으로 구성되며, 각 쌍은 &로 구분됩니다. 예를 들면 다음과 같습니다:[CODE_BLOCK_0]여기서 keyword, category, page, sortName은 각각 쿼리 문자열의 키(key)이고, apple, fruits, 1, asc는 그에 해당하는 값(value)입니다.URLSearchParams 객체를 사용하면 이러한 쿼리 문자열을 쉽게 다룰 수 있습니다. 위의 코드에서 보이는 것처럼, URLSearchParams 생성자를 사용하여 현재 URL의 쿼리 문자열을 파싱하고, .get() 메서드를 사용하여 특정 키에 해당하는 값을 가져올 수 있습니다.예를 들어, 위의 코드에서:keyword, category, currentPage, sortName은 각각 URL의 쿼리 문자열에서 searchParams 객체를 통해 해당 키의 값을 가져오는 데 사용됩니다.따라서, URLSearchParams 객체를 사용하면 JavaScript 코드에서 URL의 쿼리 파라미터를 손쉽게 추출하고 조작할 수 있습니다.

Conversations.Prompt: 이런 td 안에 체크 박스를 넣고, 컨트롤러로 보낼 때는 체크 박스에서 체크된 값을 모아서 받을 수 있어?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPT네, 이 HTML 코드는 체크 박스를 포함하는 테이블을 정의하고 있습니다. 각각의 <td> 요소에는 고유한 ID가 할당되어 있으며, 이 ID를 사용하여 JavaScript를 통해 해당 체크 박스의 상태를 가져올 수 있습니다. 사용자가 체크 박스를 선택하면, 선택된 값을 컨트롤러로 보내는 데 사용할 수 있습니다.아래는 JavaScript를 사용하여 체크 박스의 상태를 가져오고 컨트롤러로 보내는 방법에 대한 예시입니다:[CODE_BLOCK_0]위의 코드는 각 체크 박스의 상태 변화를 감지하고 선택된 체크 박스의 ID를 selectedAllergies 배열에 추가 또는 제거하는 방식으로 작동합니다. 이후에 sendSelectedAllergiesToController 함수에서 선택된 체크 박스 값을 컨트롤러로 보내는 로직을 수행하면 됩니다. 이 예시는 선택된 체크 박스 값을 로그에 출력하고 있지만, 실제로는 서버로 데이터를 전송하도록 수정해야 합니다.

Conversations.Prompt: 내가 보낸 건 그냥 테이블인데? 각 <td>에 체크 박스를 넣고 공통된 name을 준다면 배열로 가능한가?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPT네, 가능합니다. 각 <td> 요소에 체크 박스를 넣고 동일한 name 속성을 부여하면, 그룹화된 체크 박스의 값이 배열로 전송될 수 있습니다. 이를 이용하여 사용자가 선택한 체크 박스의 값을 배열로 받아 컨트롤러로 전송할 수 있습니다.아래는 해당 방법을 구현한 예시입니다:[CODE_BLOCK_0]여기서 name="allergies[]"는 모든 체크 박스를 하나의 그룹으로 묶어주는 역할을 합니다. []는 배열 형태로 여러 값을 전송하기 위한 표기법입니다.이제 선택된 체크 박스의 값을 폼을 제출할 때, 선택한 값들이 allergies[]라는 이름으로 배열로 전송될 것입니다. 이 데이터를 서버로 전송하거나 JavaScript를 사용하여 처리할 수 있습니다.서버 측에서는 선택된 값들을 배열로 받아 처리하는 방식으로 구현하면 됩니다. 예를 들어 PHP에서는 다음과 같이 받을 수 있습니다:[CODE_BLOCK_1]JavaScript를 사용하여 데이터를 처리할 경우, FormData 객체를 사용하여 폼 데이터를 수집하고 전송할 수 있습니다.

기본적으로 Ubuntu에서는 sudo 명령을 실행할 수 있는 사용자 목록이 /etc/sudoers 파일에 정의됩니다. 사용자를 sudo 그룹에 추가하면 해당 사용자는 sudo 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.사용자를 sudo 그룹에 추가하려면 다음 명령을 사용합니다:[CODE_BLOCK_2]여기서 your_username은 권한을 부여하려는 사용자의 이름입니다.로그아웃 및 다시 로그인:

Conversations.Prompt: 지금 파일서버와 연동해야 하는 계정인데 권한이 없어서 그래
Conversations.Answer:
ChatGPT파일 서버와 연동해야 하는 계정에 대한 권한을 관리자로 변경하려면 root 권한을 가진 사용자 또는 시스템 관리자에게 요청하여 권한을 변경해야 합니다. 권한을 변경하는 과정은 시스템 보안을 위해 신중하게 처리되어야 하므로 주의 깊게 진행되어야 합니다.관리자에게 권한을 부여하거나 변경하는 방법은 다음과 같습니다:루트 권한을 가진 사용자 (root)로 로그인:

원하는 사용자 계정에 대한 권한을 변경합니다. 일반적으로는 chmod 명령어를 사용하여 파일 또는 디렉토리에 대한 권한을 변경하거나, chown 명령어를 사용하여 파일 또는 디렉토리의 소유자를 변경할 수 있습니다.예를 들어, user1 계정에 대한 권한을 변경하려면:[CODE_BLOCK_0]또는[CODE_BLOCK_1]위의 명령어에서 /path/to/user1_directory는 사용자 user1의 디렉토리 경로를 나타냅니다.시스템 보안 정책을 준수:

권한 변경 작업을 완료한 후 로그아웃하고 다시 필요한 계정으로 로그인합니다.권한 변경 작업은 신중하게 고려되어야 하며, 필요한 경우 시스템 관리자 또는 보안 전문가에게 의뢰하여 작업하는 것이 좋습니다. 또한 권한 변경에 대한 작업 로그를 남기고, 권한 변경 사항을 주기적으로 검토하여 보안을 유지하는 것이 중요합니다.

ListOfCode.Content: chmod +rwx /path/to/user1_directory
chown user1:user1 /path/to/user1_directory

Conversations.Prompt: root로 로그인하고 ubuntu 라는 계정의 권한을 올리고 싶다니까. filezila 연동이 안 돼
Conversations.Answer:
ChatGPTUbuntu 시스템에서 root로 로그인하고 ubuntu 계정의 권한을 변경하여 FileZilla 또는 다른 FTP 클라이언트를 사용할 수 있도록 하는 것은 권장되지 않습니다. 보안상의 이유로 root 계정을 사용하는 것은 위험하며, 특정 사용자에게 FTP 접근 권한을 부여하는 것이 더 안전한 방법입니다.FTP 접근 권한을 부여하기 위해 다음 단계를 따르는 것이 좋습니다:FTP 서버 설치 및 설정:
먼저 Ubuntu 시스템에 FTP 서버 (예: vsftpd, proftpd 등)를 설치하고 설정합니다. 다음은 vsftpd를 예로 든 것입니다.[CODE_BLOCK_0]FTP 서버를 설치하고 나면 설정 파일(/etc/vsftpd.conf)을 편집하여 필요한 변경 사항을 적용합니다. 예를 들어, 사용자 접근을 허용하도록 설정합니다.FTP 사용자 추가:
FTP 서버에 접근할 수 있는 사용자를 추가하고, 해당 사용자에게 FTP 디렉토리의 권한을 부여합니다. 사용자를 추가하려면 adduser 명령어를 사용합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_1]your_ftp_user에는 원하는 사용자 이름을 지정합니다. 계정이 생성되면 해당 사용자의 홈 디렉토리(/home/your_ftp_user)에 FTP 파일을 저장할 수 있습니다.FTP 디렉토리 권한 설정:
FTP 사용자가 접근할 디렉토리의 권한을 설정합니다. 일반적으로 FTP 홈 디렉토리의 소유자를 해당 FTP 사용자로 변경하고 필요한 권한을 부여합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_2]FTP 서버 재시작:
변경 사항을 적용하기 위해 FTP 서버를 재시작합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_3]FTP 클라이언트 사용:
이제 FTP 클라이언트 (예: FileZilla)를 사용하여 your_ftp_user 계정으로 서버에 접속할 수 있습니다. FTP 서버 주소와 포트 번호, 사용자 이름 및 비밀번호를 설정하고 접속합니다.이렇게 하면 보안상 더 안전한 방식으로 FTP 서버에 접근 권한을 부여할 수 있습니다. root 계정을 사용하여 파일 서버에 접근하는 것은 위험을 초래할 수 있으므로 피하는 것이 좋습니다.

ListOfCode.Content:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install vsftpd
sudo adduser your_ftp_user

sudo chown -R your_ftp_user:your_ftp_user /home/your_ftp_user
sudo chmod -R 755 /home/your_ftp_user
sudo service vsftpd restart

SQL에서 원하는 결과를 직접 얻을 수 있으며, 중복된 데이터를 가져오지 않기 때문입니다. 다음은 SQL로 처리하는 예시입니다:[CODE_BLOCK_0]이 경우, specific_column에서 'excluded_value1' 또는 'excluded_value2'와 일치하는 행을 제외하고 원하는 결과를 얻을 수 있습니다.2번의 쿼리로 처리: 한 쿼리로 모든 데이터를 가져온 다음 클라이언트 측에서 특정 칼럼을 검사하여 데이터를 제외하는 방법입니다. 이 방법은 SQL 쿼리를 2번 실행하는 것보다는 덜 효율적일 수 있습니다. 또한 대용량 데이터 검색 시 성능 문제를 야기할 수 있습니다.값을 여러개 보내서 한 번에 처리: 검색 조건을 여러 개의 값으로 보내고, 서버 측에서 이러한 조건을 이용하여 하나의 쿼리로 데이터를 가져오고 필터링하는 방법입니다. 이 방법은 두 번의 쿼리를 실행하는 것보다 효율적일 수 있으며, 중복 데이터를 줄일 수 있습니다.어떤 방법을 선택할지는 다음을 고려해야 합니다:데이터 양: 대량의 데이터를 처리해야 하는 경우 성능을 고려하여 SQL로 처리하는 것이 일반적으로 좋습니다.서버 및 클라이언트 성능: 서버와 클라이언트의 성능을 고려하여 최적의 방법을 선택합니다.유지 보수성: 코드의 가독성 및 유지 보수성을 고려하여 결정합니다.데이터베이스 종류: 사용하는 데이터베이스 시스템에 따라 최적의 방법이 다를 수 있습니다.최종 결정은 프로젝트의 요구 사항 및 성능 특성에 따라 다를 것이므로, 상황에 맞게 선택하십시오.

SELECT *
FROM your_table
WHERE your_condition
AND specific_column NOT IN ('excluded_value1', 'excluded_value2');

Conversations.Prompt: 그러면 sqlsessiontemplate을 통해서 selectlist를 실행할 때, keyword와 filter를 보내서 keyword를 통해 조회한 값에서 filter에 해당되는 걸 제거해서 반환하게끔 하려면 어떻게 해야 할까? 예시와 구문, 주석을 통해 알려줘
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTSQLSessionTemplate를 사용하여 MyBatis를 통해 데이터베이스에서 데이터를 조회한 후, 검색된 결과에서 특정 조건(예: filter)에 따라 데이터를 제거하고 반환하려면 다음과 같은 단계를 따를 수 있습니다. 아래 예시는 MyBatis와 Java를 기반으로 하며, 검색 결과를 처리하는 방법을 보여줍니다. 주석을 통해 각 단계를 설명합니다.Mapper Interface 작성: MyBatis에서 SQL 쿼리를 정의하고 해당 쿼리를 호출하는 메서드를 가지는 Mapper 인터페이스를 작성합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_0]Mapper XML 작성: SQL 쿼리를 Mapper XML 파일에 정의합니다. 이때 keyword를 사용하여 데이터를 검색하고, filter에 해당하는 조건에 따라 데이터를 필터링할 쿼리를 작성합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_1]이 쿼리에서 filter는 Java 코드에서 전달할 리스트 형태의 필터링 조건입니다.Service 클래스: 검색 및 데이터 처리를 위한 Service 클래스를 작성합니다. Service 클래스에서는 Mapper 인터페이스를 호출하고 결과를 필터링합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_2]Controller: Controller에서는 검색과 필터링을 위한 API 엔드포인트를 작성하고 Service를 호출합니다.[CODE_BLOCK_3]이제 /search 엔드포인트로 요청을 보내면 검색어(keyword)와 필터(filter)를 전달하고, 해당 검색 결과에서 필터에 해당하는 데이터가 제거된 결과를 얻을 수 있습니다. Java와 MyBatis를 사용하여 데이터베이스 조회 및 필터링을 수행하는 예시입니다.

<select id="searchSnacks" resultType="your.package.Snack">
    SELECT *
    FROM your_table
    WHERE name LIKE CONCAT('%', #{keyword}, '%')

            #{item}
        </foreach>

Conversations.Answer: ChatGPT감사합니다. 결과가 SearchDTO 타입으로 반환되고 filter가 String[] 타입인 경우 다음과 같이 수정할 수 있습니다.Service 클래스 수정:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Controller 수정:[CODE_BLOCK_1]이제 /search 엔드포인트로 요청을 보내면 검색어 (keyword) 및 필터 (filter)를 전달하고, 해당 검색 결과에서 필터에 해당하는 데이터가 제거된 SearchDTO 리스트를 얻을 수 있습니다. 이 코드는 Arrays.asList(filter)를 사용하여 필터링에 필요한 데이터를 비교하고 제거하는 방식으로 작동합니다.

Conversations.Prompt: 배열에 해당하는 걸 다 대조해야지 없앨 수 있지 않아? 반복되는 구문이 있나? 내가 람다식을 잘 몰라서 이해를 못한 것일 수도 있어
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPT네, 배열에 해당하는 값을 대조하여 없앨 수 있습니다. 람다식을 사용하면 반복문을 명시적으로 작성하지 않고도 간결하게 요소를 검사하고 제거할 수 있습니다.위의 코드에서 searchResults.removeIf(snack -> Arrays.asList(filter).contains(snack.getSpecificColumn())); 부분을 설명해드리겠습니다:searchResults.removeIf 메서드는 리스트에서 조건을 만족하는 요소를 제거합니다.snack -> Arrays.asList(filter).contains(snack.getSpecificColumn())는 람다식입니다. 이 람다식은 searchResults 리스트의 각 SearchDTO 요소를 검사하고 해당 요소의 getSpecificColumn() 값이 filter 배열에 포함되어 있는지 확인합니다.람다식을 사용하면 배열과 List를 반복적으로 비교하고 일치하는 요소를 찾을 때 명시적인 반복문을 작성할 필요가 없으므로 코드가 간결해집니다. 이 코드는 filter 배열에 있는 값들과 SearchDTO의 특정 열을 비교하여 일치하는 경우 해당 SearchDTO를 제거합니다.

Conversations.Prompt: snack은 어떤 의미야?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTsnack은 여기서 SearchDTO 객체의 각 요소를 가리킵니다. 즉, searchResults 리스트에 포함된 각 SearchDTO 객체를 순회하면서 해당 객체의 특정 열(column)을 비교하여 조건을 만족하는 경우에 이를 제거하는 작업을 수행하는 데 사용됩니다. 'snack'이라는 용어는 코드에서 'SearchDTO' 객체를 가리키는 간단한 명칭으로 사용되고 있습니다.

Conversations.Prompt:
I'd like to develop my own extensible zsh configuration. I've used oh-my-zsh for years but recently ran into an issue with tab completion that I didn't even know where to start to debug. As I reviewed alternative options to oh-my-zsh I realized that I probably don't even need a plugin manager or "framework" at all. I just need to buckle down and write my own.

That's where you come in. :)

Can you please help me write an extensible, well-organized, simple, and clean zsh configuration? I'll be placing it in my existing configuration files git repository, which is always cloned to the path in $CONF_REPO, which will be set by the user at the top of .zshrc.

Requirements:

  - Written entirely in zsh (obviously).

  - All management commands should be subcommands of the top-level function: `zalgz`.

  - Plugins support. Similar in spirit to zinit.

  - .zshrc should be user-configurable options, plugin setup, etc. The main implementation should live in its own file that will be sourced from ~/.zshrc. The provided ~/.zshrc should include comments with instructions for things like plugin management, etc.

  - Autocompletion for the zalgz command itself (subcommand completion).

Please find details for these high-level requirements below.

## Plugins management

Subcommands: load, update-all

Rather than using something like git submodules, I kind of like the idea of keeping a "database" of installed plugins in a text file in $CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins.txt. On startup, the zsh configuration should read that file and sync up the currently installed plugins with what's in the database. Plugins will be cloned to $CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins/<repo>/<plugin>.

The format for the plugins.txt database is as follows:

    <repo/plugin> <git_ref>

So, on start-up, each line is read, and $CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins/<repo>/<plugin> is checked for existence. If it doesn't exist, refer to the git repo and git ref from plugins.txt to clone and checkout.

### Subcommand: zalgz load

Adds a plugin to the plugins.txt database, and installs it (checks it out with git).

Desired usage:

    $ zalgz load [<repo/plugin>]

When <repo/plugin> are given, clones https://github.com/repo/plugin.git to $CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins/<repo>/<plugin>, creating parent diretories as required, and saves the plugin to the database (<repo/plugin> <git_ref>).

For example, running the following command:

    $ zalgz load romkatv/powerlevel10k

should clone https://github.com/romkatv/powerlevel10k.git to ~/CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins/romkatv/powerlevel10k, and add the following line:

    romkatv/powerlevel10k origin/master

to $CONF_FILES/zalgz/plugins.txt.

Running without a <repo/plugin>:

    $ zalgz load

will do a plugin sync (reads plugins.txt and checks out all plugins as need).

### Subcommand: zalgz update

Desired usage:

    $ zalgz update <all|repo/plugin>

Updates the specified plugin(s) (either all plugins if the string "all" is passed, otherwise repo/plugin) according to plugins.txt. Might work to just do a `git remote update` in each package and then do a `git reset --hard <git_ref>`.

Example:

    $ zalgz update all

Updates all plugins, fetching latest for each one from git.

Or you can update a single plugin:

    $ zalgz update romkatv/powerlevel10k

import pygame
from pygame.locals import *

# Inicjalizacja biblioteki Pygame
pygame.init()

# Ustawienie rozmiaru okna gry
WIDTH = 800
HEIGHT = 600
window = pygame.display.set_mode((WIDTH, HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("Prosta platformówka")

# Kolory
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
BLUE = (0, 0, 255)

# Stałe dotyczące postaci
PLAYER_WIDTH = 50
PLAYER_HEIGHT = 50
PLAYER_VELOCITY = 5
JUMP_VELOCITY = 10
GRAVITY = 0.5

# Pozycja początkowa postaci
player_x = 50
player_y = HEIGHT - PLAYER_HEIGHT

# Tworzenie prostokątów-platform
platforms = [
    pygame.Rect(0, HEIGHT - 20, WIDTH, 20),
    pygame.Rect(200, HEIGHT - 100, 100, 20),
    pygame.Rect(400, HEIGHT - 200, 150, 20),
    pygame.Rect(600, HEIGHT - 300, 100, 20)
]

# Zmienne dotyczące ruchu postaci
player_velocity_y = 0
is_jumping = False

# Główna pętla gry
running = True
while running:
    # Sprawdzanie zdarzeń
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == QUIT:
            running = False

    # Poruszanie postaci
    keys = pygame.key.get_pressed()
    if keys[K_LEFT] and player_x > 0:
        player_x -= PLAYER_VELOCITY
    if keys[K_RIGHT] and player_x < WIDTH - PLAYER_WIDTH:
        player_x += PLAYER_VELOCITY
    if keys[K_SPACE] and not is_jumping:
        is_jumping = True
        player_velocity_y = -JUMP_VELOCITY

    # Implementacja grawitacji
    player_velocity_y += GRAVITY
    player_y += player_velocity_y

    # Sprawdzanie kolizji z platformami
    for platform in platforms:
        if player.colliderect(platform):
            # Jeżeli postać dotyka platformy, zatrzymujemy skok
            if player_velocity_y > 0:
                player_y = platform.y - PLAYER_HEIGHT
                player_velocity_y = 0
                is_jumping = False
            break

    # Rysowanie tła i postaci
    window.fill(WHITE)
    player = pygame.Rect(player_x, player_y, PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT)
    pygame.draw.rect(window, BLUE, player)

    # Rysowanie platform
    for platform in platforms:
        pygame.draw.rect(window, BLUE, platform)

    # Aktualizacja okna gry
    pygame.display.update()

# Zakończenie gry
pygame.quit()

#!/bin/bash

# Folder containing images
dir="/path/to/your/directory"

temp_dir=$(mktemp -d -p /tmp image_links.XXXXXX)

while true
do
    # Clean up the old links

    # Load the new allowed tags from a file
    mapfile -t allowed_tags < /path/to/your/tags/file

    # Set the modification time to the capture time
    for img in "$dir"/*
    do
        jhead -ft "$img"
    done

    do
        for img in $(exiftool -q -r -if '$Keywords =~ /'"$tag"'/i' -p '$Directory/$FileName' "$dir")
        do
            ln -s "$img" "$temp_dir"
        done
    done

    # Display images from the temporary directory
    feh -r -S mtime -D 5 "$temp_dir"
    sleep 1

    # Wait for 24 hours before the next iteration
    sleep 86400
done

Conversations.Prompt: Should I ever source a script to execute it from within another script as opposed to just using ./script.sh?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTWhether you should source a script (source script.sh or . script.sh) or execute it (./script.sh) depends on what you want to achieve.Sourcing a script (source script.sh or . script.sh): This reads and executes commands from the filename argument in the current shell context. If the script sets environmental variables or changes the current directory, these changes will be reflected in the shell that sourced the script. This is often used for loading environment variables or shell configuration from a script.Executing a script (./script.sh): This runs the script in a new shell process. Any environmental variables set or directory changes made in the script will not affect the calling shell. This is the usual way to run scripts that perform a series of commands and don't need to modify the environment of the calling shell.So, if you want the script to modify the environment of the calling script (for example, setting environment variables), use source. If you want the script to perform actions (like processing data) and its environment changes shouldn't affect the calling script, use ./.Remember that scripts need to have execute permissions (chmod +x script.sh) to be run with ./. Sourcing a script with source or . doesn't require execute permissions, as it's read and executed by the current shell.

import PySimpleGUI as sg
from googletrans import Translator, LANGUAGES

def translate_text(text, target="en"):
    translator = Translator()
    translation = translator.translate(text, dest=target)
    return translation.text

def create_window():
    sg.theme('LightGreen')

    layout = [
        [sg.Text('Choose a language to translate to:'),
         sg.Combo(list(LANGUAGES.values()), key='-LANG-', size=(20, 1))],
        [sg.Text('Enter text to translate:'),
         sg.InputText(key='-TEXT-', size=(50, 5))],
        [sg.Button('Translate'), sg.Button('Exit')],
        [sg.Text('Translation output:', size=(40, 1))],
        [sg.Output(size=(60, 10), key='-OUTPUT-')]
    ]

    return sg.Window('Text Translator', layout, font=('Helvetica', 14))

def main():
    window = create_window()

    while True:
        event, values = window.read()

        if event == sg.WINDOW_CLOSED or event == 'Exit':
            break

        if event == 'Translate':
            target_language_key = {v: k for k, v in LANGUAGES.items()}[values['-LANG-']]
            translated_text = translate_text(values['-TEXT-'], target=target_language_key)
            print(translated_text)

    window.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import PySimpleGUI as sg
from googletrans import Translator, LANGUAGES

def translate_text(text, target="en"):
    translator = Translator()
    translation = translator.translate(text, dest=target)
    return translation.text

def create_window():
    sg.theme('LightGreen')

    layout = [
        [sg.Text('Choose a language to translate to:'),
         sg.InputText(key='-SEARCH-', enable_events=True, size=(20, 1)),
         sg.Combo(list(LANGUAGES.values()), key='-LANG-', size=(20, 1), readonly=True)],
        [sg.Text('Enter text to translate:'),
         sg.InputText(key='-TEXT-', size=(50, 5))],
        [sg.Button('Translate'), sg.Button('Exit')],
        [sg.Text('Translation output:', size=(40, 1))],
        [sg.Output(size=(60, 10), key='-OUTPUT-')]
    ]

    return sg.Window('Text Translator', layout, font=('Helvetica', 14))

def main():
    window = create_window()

    while True:
        event, values = window.read()

        if event == sg.WINDOW_CLOSED or event == 'Exit':
            break

        if event == 'Translate':
            target_language_key = {v: k for k, v in LANGUAGES.items()}[values['-LANG-']]
            translated_text = translate_text(values['-TEXT-'], target=target_language_key)
            print(translated_text)
            
        if event == '-SEARCH-':
            search_term = values['-SEARCH-'].lower()
            filtered_languages = [lang for lang in LANGUAGES.values() if search_term in lang.lower()]
            window['-LANG-'].update(values=filtered_languages)

    window.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import PySimpleGUI as sg
from translate import translate_text, LANGUAGES

def create_window():
    sg.theme("LightGreen")

    layout = [
        [
            sg.Text("Choose a language to translate to:"),
            sg.Combo(list(LANGUAGES.values()), key="-LANG-", size=(20, 1)),
        ],
        [sg.Text("Enter text to translate:"), sg.InputText(key="-TEXT-", size=(50, 5))],
        [sg.Button("Translate"), sg.Button("Exit")],
        [sg.Text("Translation output:", size=(40, 1))],
        [sg.Listbox(values=[], size=(60, 10), key="-OUTPUT-", font=("Helvetica", 12))],
    ]

    return sg.Window("Text Translator", layout, font=("Helvetica", 14))


def main():
    window = create_window()
    
    # List to store translations in the format "original - translated"
    translations = []

    while True:
        event, values = window.read()

        if event == sg.WINDOW_CLOSED or event == "Exit":
            break

        if event == "Translate":
            target_language_key = {v: k for k, v in LANGUAGES.items()}[values["-LANG-"]]

            # Create a new entry for the translation
            translation_entry = f"{values['-TEXT-']} - {translated_text}"
            
            # Insert the new entry at the beginning of the translations list
            translations.insert(0, translation_entry)

            window['-OUTPUT-'].update(translations)

    window.close()

    main()

from sqlmodel import Field, SQLModel, create_engine, Session

class Translation(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    original_text: str
    translated_text: str
    target_language: str

def create_db_and_tables():
    # Create an SQLite database file named translations.db
    engine = create_engine("sqlite:///translations.db")
    
    # Create tables in the database
    SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)
    
    return engine

def get_translation(original_text: str, target_language: str, session: Session):
    translation = session.get(Translation, (original_text, target_language))
    return translation

def add_translation(original_text: str, translated_text: str, target_language: str, session: Session):
    translation = Translation(
        original_text=original_text,
        translated_text=translated_text,
        target_language=target_language
    )
    session.add(translation)
    session.commit()

# Github PR Fetch Extension for Firefox

This is a simple Firefox extension that adds a 'git fetch' command to GitHub pull request pages, making it easy to fetch and check out pull requests locally.

## How to use

1. Clone this repository: `git clone https://github.com/<YourUsername>/Github_PR_Fetch_Extension.git`

2. Open Firefox, and enter `about:debugging` in the URL bar.

3. Click "This Firefox" (in newer versions of Firefox) or "Load Temporary Add-on" (in older versions).

4. Open the `Github_PR_Fetch_Extension` directory and select any file inside the directory.

The extension should now be temporarily installed, and you'll see it listed in your add-ons.

When you visit a pull request page on GitHub, e.g., `https://github.com/<user>/<repo>/pull/<number>`, you will find the git fetch command just below the discussion header. A copy button is provided for convenience.

## Uninstall

If you want to uninstall the extension, go to `about:debugging`, click on "This Firefox", find the extension in the list, and click "Remove".

## Support

Please [open an issue](https://github.com/<YourUsername>/Github_PR_Fetch_Extension/issues/new) for support.

Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTThe issue you're facing where the last flex item in a row overflows to the next row is because of how the browser calculates the width of flex items and rounding issues. Your temporary solution of subtracting 1 from theGridItself.clientWidth is a common approach to deal with this problem. However, there's another way to solve this issue without hardcoding the -1. You can use calc to calculate the width with a percentage-based approach.Here's how you can modify your drawGrid function to use the calc method:[CODE_BLOCK_0]By setting flexBasis to calc(100% / ${squareSideSize}), you're telling the browser to divide the container's width into equal parts based on the squareSideSize without needing to subtract 1. This should prevent the last item in a row from overflowing to the next row and give you a more accurate grid layout.This approach is more flexible because it adapts automatically to changes in container size and doesn't rely on hardcoded values.

# Junior Configuration

The Junior process can be started using the following commands:
- `npx junior-web [args]`
- `npx junior-cli [args]`
- For self-development from the git repo: `npm start -- [args]`.

## Configurations

- **--ignore, JUNIOR_IGNORE**
  - List of items to ignore in a comma-separated format.
  - Defaults to: .git, node_modules, ./prompt, and many more. Check the getIgnoreList function for the full default list.
  - The final ignore list is a combination of the default list, command line arguments, and environmental variables.
  - Example: --ignore=./pathToIgnore

- **--server-port, JUNIOR_SERVER_PORT**
  - The port for the server.
  - Default: 10101
  - Example: --server-port=8080

- **--host**
  - Host configuration. If provided without a value, it enables the host. Otherwise, specify an IP.
  - Example: --host or --host=192.168.1.2

- **-d, --dry-run** (CLI Only)
  - Runs the application in dry run mode. Please note: the CLI is not fully functional at this time.

- **--model**
  - Specifies the model to be used.
  - Default: gpt-4
  - Example: --model=gpt-5

- **--noaudit**
  - Disables the audit trail.

- **--frontend-port, JUNIOR_FRONTEND_PORT**
  - The port for the frontend.
  - Default: 5864
  - Example: --frontend-port=8081

- **--system-prompt, -s** (CLI Only)
  - Forces the system prompt. Please note: the CLI is not fully functional at this time.

## Examples

### Hosting on a VPN IP
```
npx junior-web --host=192.168.1.2
```

### Ignoring a Directory from Attention Scan
```
npx junior-cli --ignore=./myDirectory
```

# Web Interface

Junior's web interface was designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key.

## Architecture

The web interface is composed of two different servers: a frontend and a backend. The frontend server runs on port 5864, and the backend server runs on port 10101.

## Starting the Web Interface

Run the application with `npx junior-web` from your project or with `npm start` from Junior itself. A web browser window will automatically open at `http://localhost:5864`, which is where you can access the web interface.

For configuration options and details, refer to the [Configuration](./config/env_or_cli.md) documentation.

## Workflow

The typical workflow begins with editing the `prompt.yaml` file in your code editor of choice (we recommend Visual Studio Code with the Junior plugin for an optimal experience). Once you're satisfied with your task setup, you proceed to the web interface for execution and monitoring.

## Usage

The web interface has a few interactive components:

![Web Interface](./screenshot.png)

- **Generate & Copy Prompt button (Blue)**: Click this to generate a task prompt based on your `prompt.yaml` file and copy it to your clipboard. The copied prompt should be pasted to ChatGPT 4 or similar for execution.

- **Paste & Execute Change button (Orange)**: Paste the response from the AI model (a shell script) into the input field and click this button to execute the changes.

- **Roll Back to Last Commit button (Red)**: If you made a mistake or aren't happy with the changes, click this button to revert to the last commit. Please note, the rollback operation preserves the `prompt.yaml` file, but drops every change since the last commit, including new files created in the meantime, even if they were not created by Junior.

- **Commit Changes button (Green)**: After you're satisfied with your changes, click this button to commit your modifications to git.

- **Terminal**: Displays the output of your command execution. It's a simple console that shows the progress of the task.

For a more detailed guide on using the web interface, refer to our video tutorial [here](https://youtu.be/W_iwry8uT7E).

Remember, you can always refer to your `prompt.yaml` file to modify the task details or attention mechanism.

Happy developing with your AI contributor!

# Developing External Projects with Junior

Install Junior as a development dependency by running the following command:

```
npm add @aijunior/dev --save-dev
```
Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

You can initialize the necessary files in the repository with the command:

```
npx junior-init
```

This will create the following files:

```
.gitignore
prompt/projectSpecifics.md
prompt.yaml
```

The Task Interaction Files (TIF) will be gitignored:

  - `prompt.md`, the generated prompt by Junior

`prompt/projectSpecifics.md` is used to provide instructions about the codebase that Junior is working on, like preferred tools. It is important to keep this file minimal as it will be included in most prompts, and unnecessary complexity may result in the language model losing track and failing to solve the task.

npx junior-web

export function prependAndExtractLastLine(lastLine, currentData) {
  const combinedData = `${lastLine}${currentData}`;
  // Remove ANSI escape codes
  const cleanedData = combinedData.replace(/\x1B\[([0-9]{1,2}(;[0-9]{1,2})?)?[m|K]?/g, '');
  const lines = cleanedData.split('\n');
  return lines[lines.length - 1];
}

My website, https://www.scottatron.com is a static [Hugo](https://gohugo.io) site hosted on Netlify. 

The source is in a private GitHub repo, and after Netlify successfully builds and deploys the latest version, a GitHub Actions workflow is triggered which builds a PDF version of the home page and stores it as a versioned GitHub release artifact.

I'd like to automatically make the latest version of that PDF available on my website by visiting the URL https://www.scottatron.com/CV.pdf

The resulting PDF download should use the original versioned filename so that people are clear which version they're looking at if they download it.

Could you please suggest how I can achieve this using Netlify and GitHub?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTSure, you can achieve this by using a combination of GitHub Actions, Netlify Functions, and Netlify Redirects. Here's a step-by-step guide:GitHub Actions: First, you need to create a GitHub Action that triggers when a new release is created. This action should get the URL of the latest PDF artifact and store it somewhere accessible. A good option would be to store it as a JSON file in your repository.Here's an example of what this GitHub Action might look like:[CODE_BLOCK_0]This action will create a pdf-url.json file in the public directory of your repository with the URL of the latest PDF.Netlify Functions: Next, you need to create a Netlify Function that will redirect to the URL stored in the pdf-url.json file. This function will be triggered when someone visits https://www.scottatron.com/CV.pdf.Here's an example of what this function might look like:[CODE_BLOCK_1]This function should be placed in your functions directory (e.g., ./netlify/functions/redirect.js).Netlify Redirects: Finally, you need to set up a redirect in your netlify.toml file to redirect https://www.scottatron.com/CV.pdf to your Netlify Function.Here's an example of what this might look like:[CODE_BLOCK_2]This will ensure that when someone visits https://www.scottatron.com/CV.pdf, they will be redirected to the latest PDF.Please note that this is a high-level overview and you might need to adjust the code to fit your specific needs. Also, make sure to test everything in a safe environment before deploying it to production.

ListOfCode.Content:
name: Update Latest PDF URL

on:
  release:
    types: [published]

jobs:
  update_url:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Get latest release info
        id: get_info
        uses: actions/github-script@v5
        with:
          script: |
            const { data: { assets } } = await github.rest.repos.getReleaseByTag({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              tag: context.ref.replace('refs/tags/', '')
            });
            const pdfAsset = assets.find(asset => asset.name.endsWith('.pdf'));
            return pdfAsset.browser_download_url;

      - name: Update PDF URL
        run: echo '{ "url": "${{ steps.get_info.outputs.result }}" }' > ./public/pdf-url.json
        shell: bash

      - name: Commit and push
        run: |
          git config --local user.email "action@github.com"
          git config --local user.name "GitHub Action"
          git add ./public/pdf-url.json
          git commit -m "Update PDF URL" && git push

[[redirects]]
  from = "/CV.pdf"
  to = "/.netlify/functions/redirect"
  status = 302

Junior's web interface was designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key.

The web interface is composed of two different servers: a frontend and a backend. The frontend server runs on port 5864, and the backend server runs on port 10101.

Run the application with `npx junior-web` from your project or with `npm start` from Junior itself. A web browser window will automatically open at `http://localhost:5864`, which is where you can access the web interface.

        if mod_time > most_recent_time:
            most_recent_time = mod_time

        # Load the workbook

            if 'dashboard' in sheet.lower():

                # Load the data into a DataFrame using pandas
                df = pd.read_excel(file, sheet_name=sheet)

                # Extract data from row 8 to 37 of the third column (column 'C' in Excel)
                column_data = df.iloc[7:37, 2]

                # Add the data to the final DataFrame

# Add a 'Total' column as the first column of the DataFrame
dataframe.insert(0, 'Total', dataframe.sum(axis=1))

# If there was at least one .xlsm file
if most_recent_file is not None:
    # Load the workbook
    workbook = openpyxl.load_workbook(most_recent_file, data_only=True)

        if 'dashboard' in sheet.lower():
            # Load the data into a DataFrame

            column_b_data = df.iloc[7:37, 1]

#!/bin/bash

# @param $1 enable|disable
# @param $2 extension name
# @param $3 repository path [optional]

action_type="$1"
extension_name="$2"
extension_repository_path="$3"
extension_folder="$HOME/.local/share/gnome-shell/extensions/$extension_repository_path/"

echo "=== GNOME Extension Installer ==="

echo "Installing GNOME extension \"$extension_name\"..."

if [ "$action_type" == "enable" ]; then
    if [ -z "$extension_repository_path" ]; then
        if [ -d "$extension_folder" ]; then
            if [ -d "$extension_folder.git" ]; then
                echo "Pulling changes from git..."
                (cd "$extension_folder" && git pull) || exit 1
            else
                echo "No git repository. Extension will not be updated."
            fi
        else
            echo "Cloning repository..."
            git clone "$extension_repository_path" "$extension_folder" || exit 1
        fi
        
        if [ -f "$extension_folder/Makefile" ]; then
            tmp_extension_folder="/tmp/$extension_repository_path"
            mv "$extension_folder" "$tmp_extension_folder"
            echo "Compiling extension..."
            (cd "$tmp_extension_folder" && make install) || exit 1 "Compilation failed."
            echo "Cleaning up temporary extension folder..."
            rm -fr "$tmp_extension_folder" || exit 1
        else
            echo "No Makefile found. Skipping compilation..."
        fi
    fi
    
    echo "Enabling GNOME extension \"$extension_name\"..."
    gnome-extensions enable "$extension_name" || exit 1
fi

if [ "$action_type" == "disable" ]; then
    echo "Disabling GNOME extension \"$extension_name\"..."
    gnome-extensions disable "$extension_name" || exit 1
fi

echo "Installation complete."

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](docs/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://youtu.be/NL4uFJSvfW0)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*

## Description

Junior is an AI-first IDE designed from the ground up to leverage language models. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

Use a slightly different query to work around this.

Conversations.Prompt:
The following query in Postgres:
```
		DELETE FROM timeouts
		WHERE last_seen < $1
		RETURNING peer, game, lobbies
		LIMIT 1
```
Returns
```
syntax error at or near "LIMIT" (SQLSTATE 42601)
``
How do I fix this?
Conversations.Answer: ChatGPTThe DELETE statement in PostgreSQL does not support a LIMIT clause directly. The error you're seeing is due to the presence of the LIMIT 1 clause in your DELETE statement.To delete a limited number of rows, you can use a Common Table Expression (CTE) with the DELETE statement. Here's a way you can modify your query to delete a single row (similar to using LIMIT 1) based on your provided conditions:[CODE_BLOCK_0]This CTE selects the first row matching your condition, then deletes only that row from the timeouts table.Do note that this approach can be less performant than a straightforward DELETE when working with large tables, but for small operations, the difference is often negligible. If you frequently find yourself needing to delete a small number of rows based on complex criteria, this method should be suitable.

ListOfCode.Content:
WITH deleted_rows AS (
    SELECT peer, game, lobbies 
    FROM timeouts
    WHERE last_seen < $1
    LIMIT 1
)
DELETE FROM timeouts
USING deleted_rows
WHERE timeouts.peer = deleted_rows.peer
AND timeouts.game = deleted_rows.game
AND timeouts.lobbies = deleted_rows.lobbies
RETURNING deleted_rows.peer, deleted_rows.game, deleted_rows.lobbies;

# Prompt Descriptor

The prompt descriptor is a YAML file (prompt.yaml) that outlines the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model. It is used to specify the task, attention, requirements, and other attributes.

## Example

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
```

## Attributes

- task: Describes the task type and scope.
- attention: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- requirements: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- format: (Optional and half-working) Determines how the output will be formatted. It should be avoided for now.
- os: (Default: "Debian") Specifies the operating system.
- installedTools: By default, this includes "npm, jq." Allows the user to mention his tools, e.g. when drawing. The user can create prompt/installedTools.md to overwrite.

### Overwriting Attributes

Users can overwrite attributes in prompt.yaml or create prompt/attributeName.md with the content for any attribute. If both are present, the value in prompt.yaml has preference.

For example, to set a default operating system in a separate file:

```markdown
# prompt/os.md
Debian
```

And then to overwrite it in the prompt.yaml:

```yaml
os: Ubuntu
```

## Attributes referencing .md files

When a yaml attribute refers to an existing file, its content will be used. For example, the line `task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md` in the example yaml refers to an existing markdown file and its content is injected into the task section of the prompt.

## Template Files

```
Implement the following feature!

- Create a plan!
- Create new files when needed!

Requirements:

<%= requirements %>

<%= projectSpecifics %>
```

Prompt parts are markdown template files, and [ejs](https://ejs.co/) runs on them. Attributes from the yaml file are available in the template, e.g., `<%= requirements %>` injects the requirements.

## Custom Attributes

The user can also define custom attributes not listed above. These can be stored in a markdown file and can be injected into prompt template files using the ejs syntax.

For example, to set a new custom attribute called "documentationRequirements":

```markdown
# prompt/documentationRequirements.md
Ensure that all functions are documented.
```

And then it can be injected into the prompt template:

```
<%= documentationRequirements %>
```
```

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [docs/web.md](docs/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Description

Junior is an AI-first IDE designed from the ground up to leverage language models. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [docs/web.md](docs/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

# Web Interface

Junior's web interface was designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key.

## Architecture

The web interface is composed of two different servers: a frontend and a backend. The frontend server runs on port 5864, and the backend server runs on port 10101.

## Starting the Web Interface

Run the application with `junior-web` from your project. A web browser window will automatically open at `http://localhost:5864`, which is where you can access the web interface.

For configuration options and details, refer to the [Configuration](./config/env_or_cli.md) documentation.

## Workflow

The typical workflow begins with editing the `prompt.yaml` file in your code editor of choice (we recommend Visual Studio Code with the Junior plugin for an optimal experience). Once you're satisfied with your task setup, you proceed to the web interface for execution and monitoring.

## Usage

The web interface has a few interactive components:

![Web Interface](./screenshot.png)

- **Generate & Copy Prompt button (Blue)**: Click this to generate a task prompt based on your `prompt.yaml` file and copy it to your clipboard. The copied prompt should be pasted to ChatGPT 4 or similar for execution.

- **Paste & Execute Change button (Orange)**: Paste the response from the AI model (a shell script) into the input field and click this button to execute the changes.

- **Roll Back to Last Commit button (Red)**: If you made a mistake or aren't happy with the changes, click this button to revert to the last commit. Please note, the rollback operation preserves the `prompt.yaml` file, but drops every change since the last commit, including new files created in the meantime, even if they were not created by Junior.

- **Commit Changes button (Green)**: After you're satisfied with your changes, click this button to commit your modifications to git.

- **Terminal**: Displays the output of your command execution. It's a simple console that shows the progress of the task.

For a more detailed guide on using the web interface, refer to our video tutorial [here](https://youtu.be/W_iwry8uT7E).

Remember, you can always refer to your `prompt.yaml` file to modify the task details or attention mechanism.

Happy developing with your AI contributor!

```

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { execSync } from 'child_process';
import { createPromptYaml } from './prompt/createPromptYaml.js';
import { createGitignore } from './git/createGitignore.js';
import { createPromptDir } from './prompt/createPromptDir.js';
import copyDefaults from './command/init/copyDefaults.js';
import path from 'path';

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));

async function juniorInit() {
  execSync('git init', { stdio: 'inherit' });

  createGitignore();
  await createPromptDir();
  createPromptYaml();

  // Correcting the path to the prompt/defaults folder in the installed version of Junior
  const defaultsPath = path.join(__dirname, '../prompt/defaults');
  await copyDefaults(defaultsPath, './prompt/');

  execSync('git add .', { stdio: 'inherit' });
  execSync('git commit -m "Junior init"', { stdio: 'inherit' });

  console.log('\x1b[32mRepo initialized for Junior development\x1b[0m');
}

juniorInit();

import sharp from 'sharp';
import { writeFileSync } from 'fs';

const inputSVGPath = 'docs/assets/logo.svg';
const outputPNGPath = 'docs/assets/logo.png';

const updateLogo = async () => {
  try {
    const buffer = await sharp(inputSVGPath).png().toBuffer();
    writeFileSync(outputPNGPath, buffer);
  } catch (err) {
    throw err;
  }
};

updateLogo();

```

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](docs/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [docs/web.md](docs/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

# Developing External Projects with Junior

## Installation

Install Junior as a development dependency by running the following command:

```
npm add @aijunior/dev --save-dev
```

## Initialization

You can initialize the necessary files in the repository with the command:

```
npx junior-init
```

This will create the following files:

```
.gitignore
prompt/projectSpecifics.md
prompt.yaml
```

The Task Interaction Files (TIF) will be gitignored:
  - `prompt.yaml`, the prompt descriptor filled by the user ([descriptor.md](./descriptor.md))
  - `prompt.md`, the generated prompt by Junior
  - `change.sh`, the changeset generated by the language model

### Project Specifics

`prompt/projectSpecifics.md` is used to provide instructions about the codebase that Junior is working on, like preferred tools. It is important to keep this file minimal as it will be included in most prompts, and unnecessary complexity may result in the language model losing track and failing to solve the task.

## Starting Junior

You can start Junior with:

```
npx junior-web

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](doc/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [doc/web.md](doc/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

# Web Interface

Junior's web interface was designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key.

## Architecture

The web interface is composed of two different servers: a frontend and a backend. The frontend server runs on port 5173, and the backend server runs on port 10101.

## Starting the Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start both servers. A web browser window will automatically open at `http://localhost:5173`, which is where you can access the web interface.

## Workflow

The typical workflow begins with editing the `prompt.yaml` file in your code editor of choice (we recommend Visual Studio Code with the Junior plugin for an optimal experience). Once you're satisfied with your task setup, you proceed to the web interface for execution and monitoring.

## Usage

The web interface has a few interactive components:

![Web Interface](./screenshot.png)

- **Generate & Copy Prompt button (Blue)**: Click this to generate a task prompt based on your `prompt.yaml` file and copy it to your clipboard. The copied prompt should be pasted to ChatGPT 4 or similar for execution.

- **Paste & Execute Change button (Orange)**: Paste the response from the AI model (a shell script) into the input field and click this button to execute the changes.

- **Roll Back to Last Commit button (Red)**: If you made a mistake or aren't happy with the changes, click this button to revert to the last commit. Please note, the rollback operation preserves the `prompt.yaml` file, but drops every change since the last commit, including new files created in the meantime, even if they were not created by Junior.

- **Terminal**: Displays the output of your command execution. It's a simple console that shows the progress of the task.

For a more detailed guide on using the web interface, refer to our video tutorial [here](https://youtu.be/W_iwry8uT7E).

Remember, you can always refer to your `prompt.yaml` file to modify the task details or attention mechanism.

At the end of your development, make sure to run `npm run build:doc` to regenerate the web.html document reflecting the latest changes.

Happy developing with your AI contributor!

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](docs/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [docs/web.md](docs/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

npm add @aijunior/dev --save-dev

npx junior-init

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](docs/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [docs/web.md](docs/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

# Junior - Your AI contributor which codes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](doc/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory. Additionally, you can install the "Junior" vscode extension from the vscode extension marketplace.

### Usage

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [doc/web.md](doc/web.md).

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

# Junior - Your AI contributor which writes itself.

[![Video: Junior codes itself](doc/assets/video_cover.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W_iwry8uT7E)

*"Video: Junior codes itself"*
## Description

Junior is an exploratory project aimed at revolutionizing the way programmers interact with the development process. Just like how Linus Torvalds oversees the Linux Kernel development without coding himself, this project allows developers to communicate with the AI and supervise the development process.

Isn't that already possible with ChatGPT? No, LLMs have very limited "working memory", so it is not possible to directly work with them on large codebases.

By providing specific task details in a prompt descriptor and highlighting the relevant parts of your project, you can delegate code implementation, documentation, testing, and more to your AI Junior.

## Getting Started

### Installation

To install, clone the repository and run `npm install` in the root directory.

### Usage

There are two ways to use this project: a command-line interface (CLI) and a web interface.

#### Command-line interface (CLI)

To start the CLI, use `npm run cli`. This mode uses the ChatGPT API, and you'll need an API key stored in the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable.

#### Web Interface

Run the application with `npm start` to start a local server, where you can generate a prompt and automatically copy it to paste into ChatGPT. The web interface is designed for use with ChatGPT Pro and doesn't require an API key. For more information about the web interface, please refer to [doc/web.md](doc/web.md).

### The Prompt Descriptor

A prompt descriptor is a YAML file (`prompt.yaml`) outlining the details necessary for generating a task prompt for the AI model.

Here's an example of a prompt descriptor:

```yaml
task: prompt/task/feature/implement.md
attention:
  - src/interactiveSession/startInteractiveSession.js
  - src/prompt/createPrompt.js
  - src/attention/readAttention.js
  - prompt.yaml
requirements: >
  Write a README.md for this _exploratory_ project!
format: prompt/format/new_file_version.md
```

Each element in the descriptor serves a specific purpose:
- `task`: Describes the task type and scope. For example, `feature/implement`, `bug/fix`, or `refactor/`. You can check out the [prompt/task/feature/implement.md](prompt/task/feature/implement.md) file as an example.
- `attention`: Lists the files and directories most relevant to the task.
- `requirements`: Describes the actual task in a human-readable format.
- `format`: Determines how the output will be formatted.

### Attention Mechanism

The attention mechanism guides the AI model by providing it with a working set. It helps overcome the limited working memory of large language models.

The working set is a subset of the entire project that's currently in focus. It includes both files and directories. For files, the content is directly provided to the AI. For directories, a brief list of files and subdirectories within them is presented.

## Contributing and Support

Contributions are welcome! Remember, we eat our own dog food in this project. Junior is designed to write itself. Your main role will be to oversee the work, provide detailed prompts, and review the outcomes.

For support, please create an issue in the GitHub repository.

**Note:** For meaningful results, it's recommended to use the GPT-4 model or a more recent version.

# Junior VSCode Extension

Welcome to the Junior VSCode Extension, a tool created to streamline your interaction with the [Junior project](https://github.com/tisztamo/Junior). 

Just like the rest of the Junior project, this extension and its documentation were entirely generated by ChatGPT, an advanced AI model by OpenAI. 

## How to Use the Junior VSCode Extension

This extension aids you in preparing tasks for the AI model. Here's how you use it:

1. Write your requirements into the `prompt.yaml` file.
2. Open all the files that you believe the AI will need to solve the task.
3. Activate the "Write Attention" command.

By following these steps, the extension will update the attention section of your `prompt.yaml` file, tailoring it to the files you have currently opened in your VSCode workspace.

### Write Attention Command

The "Write Attention" command, activated through `junior.writeAttention`, overwrites the attention descriptor based on the files and folders you have opened in your workspace. This allows you to guide the AI's focus towards specific areas of your project.

### Configuration

You can personalize the behavior of the Write Attention command through the VSCode settings. In the `junior` section, you'll find an `attentionExcludeList`. This is an array of glob patterns that allows you to exclude certain files or directories from being included in the `attention` field when the "Write Attention" command is used.

Get started and enjoy co-creating with the Junior AI!
